statement: If an odd number by multiplying an even number make some number, the product will be even.
heath_proof: For let the odd number A by multiplying the even number B make C; I say that C is even. For, since A by multiplying B has made C, therefore C is made up of as many numbers equal to B as there are units in A. [VII. Def. 15] And B is even; therefore C is made up of even numbers. But, if as many even numbers as we please be added together, the whole is even. [IX. 21] Therefore C is even.
ai_proof_text:
9.28
**Statement:** If an odd number by multiplying an even number make some number, the product will be even.

**Step 1.** Let the odd number A by multiplying the even number B make the number C. I say that C is even.

**Step 2.** Since A by multiplying B has made C, by the definition of multiplication [D7.15] B has been added to itself as many times as there are units in A; therefore C is made up of as many numbers equal to B as there are units in A.

**Step 3.** But B is even by hypothesis; therefore each of the numbers of which C is made up is even, and so C is made up of even numbers added together.

**Step 4.** But if as many even numbers as we please be added together, the whole is even [9.21]. Therefore C is even.

**Step 5.** Therefore, if an odd number by multiplying an even number make some number, the product will be even. Q.E.D.
